data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's evidence fails to distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance in the very case the problem targets. The claim says reliability gain is genuine if performance holds on a different distribution, but persistence under distribution shift can be produced by two very different mechanisms: a causal/expert-encoded checklist (genuine) or a low-variance, distribution-agnostic rote procedure that happens to still track the right answer on the shifted sample. The target offers no single-evaluation evidence separating these: it does not require outcome-conditional process data showing panel reasoning tracks the answer's causal determinants, nor item-level overfitting checks. Thus its own proposal does not distinguish the genuine gain from compliance that tracks the right answer under shift.
